covers: a class whose __init__ stores its model parameter in self.model, read at a request in a method, and a module-level function whose parameter is a request's model: their requests report the defaults as before
calls from another file through a relative import record the model they pass in that file: a literal, a module constant and a positional argument; a call that leaves the parameter out is not recorded
a call from a script in another directory through an absolute import, with an environment fallback (env_default plus an env_var gap)
a module attribute (sampler.Sampler) and an import of a module that is not in the project are not followed
notes: Synthetic. Truth is what each line does at run time, except where a policy turns it into a gap. evals/sampler.py:13 sends self.model, which Sampler.__init__ stores from its model parameter; :19 sends ask's model parameter. Each request still reports its default with its gaps. evals/run.py imports both with relative imports: :7 and :8 pass a literal and a module constant, :9 passes nothing (the default applies, reported in sampler.py), :10 passes ClaudeSampler's model by position, :15 passes ask's by name. scripts/bench.py imports evals.sampler absolutely from another directory and passes an environment fallback. scripts/unfollowed.py calls Sampler as a module attribute and imports a module the project does not have, so neither model is ever output.
